b300-cfg-parallel-bcg.description: B300: The default command plus breakable CUDA graphs (LTX-2/2.3 are on sglang's validated BCG list), captured at the case shape.
b300-cfg-parallel-bcg.notes: TRT-LLM's LTX-2 row runs CUDA graphs (NVIDIA's official config) at 0.044 s per stage-1 step against sglang's 0.192 s (4xB300, 2026-10-22); stage 1 is ~1.5k tokens, so the step is launch-bound. BCG replays the same kernels, so the output is unchanged. Promoted from cand-bcg by the 2026-10-22 4xB300 A/B (scripts/run_b300_ab_20261022.sh, second wave): two rounds, 3.797/3.785 s against default (eager) 6.693/6.882, gb300-cfg-parallel-compile 9.978/9.767, cand-usp2-bcg 4.613/4.573, cand-usp2 10.40/10.74. BCG replays the same kernels (outputs bitwise equal to eager on 2xH200).

blackwell-2gpu-twostage-cfg.description: Blackwell: the two-stage pipeline with CFG parallel 2, cuDNN attention.
blackwell-2gpu-twostage-cfg.notes: Every earlier vLLM-Omni LTX-2 row ran the ONE-stage LTX2Pipeline (Lightricks/LTX-2 resolves to it unless --model-class-name LTX2TwoStagePipeline is given): 40 steps at the full 768x512 against sglang's 40 at 384x256 plus a 3-step refine, so it measured a heavier workload. Its LTX recipes also default stage 1 to the LTX-2.3 official guider (STG and a modality pass, four transformer passes a step); the request pins plain CFG 4.0 like sglang's LTX-2 (ltx-pipelines LTX-2 defaults), TRT-LLM and ComfyUI, so every row does two passes a step. VALIDATION PENDING (round 2026-10-22, 4xB300).

blackwell-cudnn.description: Blackwell vLLM-Omni profile for ltx2_twostage_t2v using cuDNN attention.
blackwell-cudnn.notes: Blackwell attention choice, measured on this box 2026-09-12. FLASH_ATTN is a Hopper-only precompiled kernel -- vLLM-Omni refuses it on sm_100 with 'FLASH_ATTN was explicitly selected but is unsupported'. FLASHINFER_ATTN starts but dies under torch.compile on dynamic shapes (`AsPythonConstantNotImplementedError: SymNodeVariable() is not a constant` in the FlashInfer backend's _ensure_plan), observed on qwen-image and cosmos3 t2v; it is fine for the static image cases (zimage, flux), which are deliberately left on it. CUDNN_ATTN is exact softmax, the same precision class as the kernels the other frameworks run here, measured at 2.741s on qwen-image (vs TRTLLM_ATTN 3.274s) and already the backend minimax-h3 serves with on this box.

vllm-omni.model_override_reason: Same weights as the case (Lightricks/LTX-2). Previously pointed at rootonchair/LTX-2-19b-distilled, carried over from the pre-JSON config with no rationale: a distilled checkpoint is explicitly lossy, needs far fewer steps, and would have made this cell unfairly fast against sglang and LightX2V on the full model. vLLM-Omni itself refuses it -- 'LTX2Pipeline requires a regular non-distilled LTX checkpoint' -- which is how it surfaced.

lightx2v.reason: LightX2V cannot run the official LTX-2 two-stage workload (dev model for stage 1, distilled LoRA for the 3-step stage-2 refine): its runner loads one transformer and merges lora_configs into it at load, and the use_upsampler path reuses that same transformer for stage 2 (lightx2v/models/runners/ltx2/ltx2_runner.py at 19c19614). The profile it had did not enable the upsampler at all, so every earlier LightX2V row ran ONE stage at the full 768x512 for 40 steps -- a heavier workload than the other rows, never comparable. Audited 2026-10-22.

blackwell-fa2.description: Blackwell LightX2V LTX-2 t2av profile: same config as default with FlashAttention 2 instead of FA3.
blackwell-fa2.notes: LightX2V's default FlashAttention-3 path is a Hopper-only precompiled kernel: on B200 it loads and then dies mid-generation with 'no kernel image is available for execution on the device' (flash-attention/hopper/flash_fwd_launch_template.h), taking the server with it. FA2 is built from source for sm_100 in this venv and is the same precision class (exact softmax), matching how SGLang and vLLM-Omni are run here. Deliberately NOT SageAttention: int8 QK quantisation is a different numeric class and not a fair substitute.

default.notes: LTX2TwoStagesPipeline: stage 1 at half resolution with CFG, the learned x2 upsampler, stage 2 distilled LoRA on sigmas [0.909375, 0.725, 0.421875, 0] (3 evaluations, no CFG); two-stage turns on when the upsampler and LoRA resolve. The model is the single BF16 file (a directory would also load the fp8/fp4 files and read the config from the alphabetically first). CUDA graphs on as in the official 4-GPU config; attention VANILLA instead of the official FA4 (Blackwell-tuned). Defaults stg_scale 0 / modality_scale 1 are plain CFG, matching sglang. VANILLA attention is torch SDPA (FlashAttention on Hopper); no cache_config or quant_config, so the row is BF16 and cache-free; compile at the case shape so the first request does not recompile; JSON to /v1/videos/sync (or /v1/images/generations), whose reply is the media itself. The YAML is passed with --visual_gen_args (trtllm-serve has no --extra_visual_gen_options). VALIDATION PENDING (round 2026-10-22, 2xH200/4xH200).

trtllm-visual.extra_env_reason: The harness exports PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True. Under it, the CUDA IPC handle TRT-LLM's rank 0 hands its media over with needs pidfd_getfd in the server process, which RunPod containers deny: every request logged 'pidfd_getfd: Operation not permitted' and hung to the read timeout (4xB300, 2026-10-22). Plain segments use cudaIpcMemHandle instead.

default.description: ComfyUI master, core nodes only, the model's official workflow with full-precision weights.
default.notes: Official video_ltx2_t2v two-stage workflow, which is the ltx-pipelines two-stage recipe sglang's LTX2TwoStagePipeline implements: stage 1 at half resolution on the full model with CFG (case guidance 4.0, negative prompt = sglang's ltx-pipelines default), latent x2 spatial upsample, stage 2 with the distilled LoRA on the same three distilled sigmas. bf16 checkpoint and Gemma-3-12B in place of fp8 / fp4_mixed; untiled VAEDecode in place of the template's tiled decode (a memory measure for small cards, and not bit-exact). Two GPUs through the MultiGPU CFG Split node on the stage-1 model, the counterpart of sglang's --enable-cfg-parallel. Weights are the full-precision single-file checkpoints ComfyUI loads (Comfy-Org repackaging or the model's own single-file release); the official template's fp8/int8/nvfp4 defaults are swapped out because they are a different numeric class from every other row. Sampler, scheduler and shift follow the official ComfyUI workflow; steps, CFG, size, frames and seed follow the case. Compile off: TorchCompileModel together with the MultiGPU CFG Split node fails on the first request (dynamo: 'Tensor device mismatch' in the stage-1 SamplerCustomAdvanced; ComfyUI 88ab4a06, 1xB200->2xB200, 2026-09-25). Splitting the two CFG branches over two cards roughly halves each step, which outweighs compile's measured 16-18% on FLUX.1, so the cell keeps the split and runs eager.
default.policy_exception: Compile broken with the CFG split, not a speed choice (2026-09-25, ComfyUI 88ab4a06, 1xB200->2xB200, see notes): TorchCompileModel with the MultiGPU CFG Split node fails the first request (dynamo 'Tensor device mismatch' in the stage-1 SamplerCustomAdvanced), and the split is worth more than compile's measured 16-18% on FLUX.1.

blackwell-gpuonly.description: Blackwell: the default graph with every model resident on the GPU (--gpu-only).
blackwell-gpuonly.notes: B200: --gpu-only keeps every model, text encoders included, stored and run on the card; a 183 GB B200 holds the largest graph here (MiniMax-H3: 62 GB DiT + 48 GB Qwen3-VL-32B + VAEs). Placement only, numerics unchanged. Measured 2026-09-25 on 1xB200, FLUX.1 eager, interleaved arms: default 5.94 / 5.77 / 5.79s against --gpu-only 5.56s and --gpu-only --disable-dynamic-vram 5.57s (Qwen-Image-2.1: 3.75 / 3.91 against 3.47 / 3.48) -- every --gpu-only arm below every default arm; disabling dynamic VRAM on top adds nothing, so the simpler flag is kept.
blackwell-gpuonly.policy_exception: Compile broken with the CFG split, not a speed choice (2026-09-25, ComfyUI 88ab4a06, 1xB200->2xB200, see the default profile's notes): TorchCompileModel with the MultiGPU CFG Split node fails the first request (dynamo 'Tensor device mismatch' in the stage-1 SamplerCustomAdvanced), and the split is worth more than compile's measured 16-18% on FLUX.1.
